transcript:
[00:00] Lena (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Lena, AE; Ravi is our SE and Ellen our CSM. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Maya (Reefline): Good thanks, a lot on the timeline so appreciate this.
[00:18] Tom (Reefline): Morning.
[00:20] Ravi (Redwood): Cool, agenda: runbook handoff, network access, perf benchmark and security artifacts. We'll go through each and collect action items.
[00:30] Maya: Sounds good. Our primary goal is to get a private deployment in staging by mid-May, production in June-ish, subject to perf.
[00:42] Lena: Okay noted, mid-May staging makes sense. Can you remind us of the constraints? Is this fully on-prem or VPC?
[00:50] Chris (Reefline): It's VPC peering into our account, we're expecting to keep logs in-region and keys in our KMS.
[00:58] Aisha (Reefline): And we need to validate network egress rules and state that data never leaves region. SOC2 is required, obvs.
[01:07] Ellen (Redwood): We'll attach our control mappings and show where Redwood fits in the attestation.
[01:12] Ravi: On the technical side, for staging we usually recommend a dedicated pool for deterministic latency. But, depending on traffic we can also route to hosted with VPC connectors. There's tradeoffs on cost/latency.
[01:27] Tom: Could you explain the difference again? We looked at the docs but some of the terms blurred.
[01:32] Ravi: Sure — dedicated capacity means reserved GPU pools you own for predictable throughput. Hosted with VPC connector is faster to spin up but multi-tenant; we still isolate data, but latency can vary more under load. Also Dedicated gives you stronger SLA.
[01:46] Maya: Latency is high priority for our agent extractor path. We need p95 below 350ms for single-turn inference. Will dedicated reliably deliver that?
[01:55] Ravi: With proper batching knobs and quantization profile, yes — we see p95 in 160–280ms for models similar to what you plan to run, depends on sequence length and KV-cache patterns. But if you have longer context it can go up.
[02:10] Maya: KV cache — do you persist that across calls? We have long-lived sessions.
[02:15] Ravi: We keep per-request KV cache in memory on the serving nodes; session-affinity helps. For persistent state you can use prefix caching or an external cache. Sometimes the transcript shows K V as separate tokens... transcription artifacts.
[02:29] Tom: Ok. On networking — Chris, what level of access will Redwood have?
[02:34] Chris: We can open peering and create a subnet for the Redwood agents. We'll give an IAM role for the deployment so they can pull images, but keys are ours.
[02:42] Aisha: We want HSM integration for the KMS if possible.
[02:46] Lena: We support customer KMS integrations; we have examples in the playbook. We'll include the KMS/HSM pattern and the mapping to our audit logs.
[02:56] Maya: About audit logs — do you stream logs to our S3 or do you store them in your console? We need log retention of 1 year.
[03:03] Ellen: We can push the audit stream to your S3 bucket or deliver via secure syslog. We'll include the retention config in the runbook.
[03:12] Tom: On the benchmark plan: what's the typical sample size? We run variable traffic across a weekend.
[03:18] Ravi: For staging we recommend 10k inference calls across representative requests, with simulated peak and steady-state windows. We'll run a baseline and then a tuned run with batching. Aim for 2–3 hours of cyclical load but we can do longer if you want.
[03:33] Maya: That aligns. We'll provide sample prompts and typical concurrency.
[03:37] Ravi: Great — please include worst-case sequence lengths. For routing, we can configure fallbacks: if Dedicated hits capacity we auto-fallback to a slightly faster model on Hosted to keep latency SLOs. Tradeoff is quality vs cost.
[03:51] Maya: Hmm, fallback worries product team a bit. How do you control regression on answers?
[03:56] Lena: We have rollout policies and can do canary tests with a percent of traffic. Redwood Optimize gives regression alerts tied to eval sets. We'll also provide the eval harness so you can run your prompts.
[04:07] Aisha: Security question — where are embeddings stored? We can't have PII persisted unencrypted.
[04:12] Ravi: Embeddings are treated like any other artifact; if you enable encryption and KMS, they're encrypted at rest. We also support ephemeral-only caching if needed.
[04:21] Maya: Great. On responsibilities — who will handle tenant mapping?
[04:25] Ellen: Redwood will draft the tenant mapping doc and invite your product/platform owners. We'll propose a schema and naming convention.
[04:33] Chris: For networking we'll need a runbook with firewall ports and approved IP ranges.
[04:37] Lena: We'll share a network checklist as part of the runbook.
[04:42] Ravi: I'm going to run through the staging benchmark assumptions now — for your sample workload we recommend these JVMs, sorry I mean these instance types, and quantization Q4_0 for latency/cost balance. Sometimes transcription says Q four zero, that's fine.
[04:58] Tom: Any prebuilt Terraform or CLI to provision connectors?
[05:02] Ellen: Yes, we have a starter Terraform module and a quickstart script. We'll drop the repo link.
[05:09] Lena: Action items recap: Lena share playbook and runbook; Ravi schedule benchmark; Ellen tenant mapping; Reefline provide traffic and SOC2/KMS docs.
[05:20] Maya: On timeline — mid-May staging still ok as long as we start the bench this week.
[05:25] Lena: We can kick off bench next Wednesday.
[05:28] Chris: One more — do you support private on-prem (air-gapped) installs? For later phases possibly.
[05:34] Ravi: We do a private deployment package; it's heavier ops but doable. We'll surface the packaging options in the playbook.
[05:41] Maya: Good. Any blockers?
[05:43] Aisha: Waiting on SOC2 doc from our vendor — but we'll try to get it. Also need to confirm KMS/HSM procurement.
[05:51] Lena: Noted. We'll keep the next touchpoint as a bench review call.
[05:55] Tom: Ok thanks everyone.
[05:58] Lena: Thanks, we'll send links and the security questionnaire after.
[06:02] Ellen: I'll set the follow-up meeting.
[06:05] Maya: Thanks all.
[06:07] [call ends]
notes: Transcript has minor ASR errors (model names, Q4_0 spoken Q four zero, KV cache split). Customer emphasized p95 latency and SOC2/KMS needs. Agreed staging benchmark and playbook handoff.
